repository.name: gothinkster/node-express-realworld-example-app
repository.workload: An actively maintained (3.8k stars, still merged into in 2026) RealWorld reference implementation. No stated production traffic.

annotation.notes: Retro-annotated from docs/evaluation.md §3.16, an independent blind pass with no memory of this project's own findings — closing the last of the deep-tier runtimes (Node.js) never independently blind-passed despite being deep-tier since before v0.2.0. Two security findings (a hardcoded JWT fallback secret; an unbounded relation include that pulls the password column into memory, though never serialized into a response) were also found and filed under Kind: Security, out of the performance rubric per SKILL.md Hard Rule 8 — not encoded here. Two real detector bugs were also found and fixed during this pass (a `sqs`/`pgx` lockfile-hash collision producing one false-positive broker signal and one accidentally-correct datastore match; and `.prisma` schema files never being scanned at all, a genuine false negative for any Prisma project with no `pg`/`postgres` token in its manifest) — both are detect_stack.py regressions, already covered by tests/test_detect_stack_regressions.py's LockfileHashCollisionTests and PrismaSchemaFileTests, not finding-content questions this schema models. `forbidden` includes the one item §3.16 documents with enough specificity to encode without inventing a location: the review correctly declined to recommend clustering/worker_threads for single-process Node.js, because no infrastructure-as-code or replica count anywhere in the repository would make a core-count claim anything but invented.

expected.mechanism: GET /articles and GET /articles/feed pass the client-supplied limit query parameter straight into Prisma's take with only a default-if-absent (Number(query.limit) || 10), never an enforced maximum. GET /articles/:slug/comments (article.service.ts:433-458) has no page bound at all. Combined with the unbounded relation fetch below, a single crafted request has no ceiling on the data it forces the service to materialize and serialize.

Every article, profile, and comment-author read fetches the ENTIRE favoritedBy and/or followedBy relation with no select, where, or take, then reduces it to a boolean in JavaScript (article.mapper.ts:11). The query already computes the efficient form in parallel -- _count: { select: { favoritedBy: true } } is present in every article query -- but articleMapper uses article.favoritedBy.length instead of the already-fetched article._count.favoritedBy: the cheap primitive is fetched and silently discarded next to the expensive one actually used.

No index on Article.authorId, Comment.articleId, or Comment.authorId anywhere in the migration history (checked in full, four files); the only non-PK/unique indexes created are on the implicit many-to-many join tables' second column. Both are on the critical-path filter/join in getArticles/getFeed/getCommentsByArticle.
Awaits two independent, unrelated findUnique calls sequentially rather than concurrently.

forbidden.why_not: technology/node.md's single-process/no-cluster/no-worker_threads guidance is explicit that under-utilized parallelism is checkable only "on a host with multiple cores available," and this repository defines no infrastructure-as-code, replica count, or host spec anywhere. Asserting the host's core count to justify a clustering recommendation would be an invented fact, not evidence -- the correct response is to decline the finding, not to report it.
